simple.meaning: צְלַח (tsᵉlach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to advance (transitive or intransitive).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 5:8. The surrounding contexts include family line, commandment, kingship, prophetic witness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צְלַח (H6744) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צְלַח (tsᵉlach) / H6744 is traced through Ezra 5:8, Ezra 6:14, Daniel 3:30, Daniel 6:29 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Be it known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in their hands.

timeline.evidenceText: Be it known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in their hands.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They built and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
